task: Repair the canonical string representation of first_source_timestamp_utc/last_source_timestamp_utc in both Parser A (qntylab/r1_reference_parser.py) and Parser B (qntylab/r1_retention_candidate.py) to conform to r1_normalized_evidence_contract_v1.json:DailyMarketEvidenceV1's own required field type ("timestamp (ISO 8601, millisecond or finer)"), per the independent NEW CHAT review of Parser A candidate commit e56b201 (verdict BLOCKED_BY_CANONICAL_FIELD_SCOPE).

frozen_protocol_binding.note: all three independently re-verified unchanged before and after this repair; this repair modifies no frozen protocol artifact, only parser implementation code

prior_review.finding: first_source_timestamp_utc/last_source_timestamp_utc are required canonical DailyMarketEvidenceV1 fields typed 'timestamp (ISO 8601, millisecond or finer)'. Parser B returned a bare Python float (not ISO-8601 at all); Parser A returned ISO-8601 but under-padded whole-second tokens to a single fractional digit instead of millisecond-or-finer. Both were prior, already-logged, still-open findings (see known_out_of_scope_findings_still_open in r1_parser_b_numeric_conformance_repair_v1.json), not sanctioned permitted provenance differences.

parser_a.location_of_fix: qntylab/r1_reference_parser.py:_epoch_to_iso -- fractional-second digit string is now zero-padded to a minimum of 3 digits (millisecond) when the source token has fewer than 3 fractional digits (including zero, i.e. a bare whole-second token); source precision finer than milliseconds is preserved verbatim, never truncated
parser_a.conformance_pre_repair: NONCONFORMING (whole-second tokens rendered as a single fractional digit, e.g. '...:36.0Z' instead of '...:36.000Z')

parser_b.location_of_fix: qntylab/r1_retention_candidate.py: added a new standalone helper _canonical_utc_timestamp(ts_decimal); daily_primitive now additionally parses Decimal(row['timestamp']) alongside the existing float(row['timestamp']) (the float is retained, unmodified, for day-boundary/cutoff checks and event-time sort ordering -- out of this repair's scope), carries the exact Decimal timestamp as a 7th tuple element through grouping/duplicate-representative-selection/sort (all of which continue to index only the pre-existing 6 elements, so this repair changes no duplicate/ordering logic), and serializes first_source_timestamp_utc/last_source_timestamp_utc from that Decimal via _canonical_utc_timestamp instead of returning the bare float
parser_b.conformance_pre_repair: NONCONFORMING (bare Python float, not ISO-8601 at all)

canonical_timestamp_rule.rule: UTC ISO-8601 string 'YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SS.fffZ', derived from the exact Decimal parse of the source epoch-seconds token (never through binary float): whole_seconds = int(ts_decimal) (truncation toward zero, unchanged from pre-existing behavior); fractional = ts_decimal - whole_seconds (exact Decimal subtraction); the fractional digit string is zero-padded on the right to a minimum of 3 digits (millisecond floor) but never truncated if the source token already carries more than 3 fractional digits.
canonical_timestamp_rule.precision_policy: millisecond-or-finer per the frozen contract's declared type; source precision beyond milliseconds (observed up to 4-6 digits on real cached objects) is preserved verbatim, never rounded or truncated

precision_firewall.claim: the canonical timestamp string is never derived by formatting a binary float; both parsers derive it from a Decimal parsed directly from the source token
precision_firewall.parser_a_evidence: _epoch_to_iso takes a Decimal parameter; parse_daily_object already parsed row['timestamp'] as Decimal (ts = _parse_decimal(row['timestamp'])) before this repair, so no new float conversion was introduced
precision_firewall.parser_b_evidence: daily_primitive now parses ts_decimal = Decimal(row['timestamp']) directly from the source string in the same try block as the pre-existing float(row['timestamp']) parse (retained, unused for canonical timestamp serialization); _canonical_utc_timestamp consumes only ts_decimal, never the float ts
precision_firewall.counterexample_checked: 1585132572.9822 (real BTCUSDT first trade): float(Decimal('1585132572.9822')) == 1585132572.9822 in this specific case (no float64 rounding is visible at this magnitude), but the canonical serialization path does not depend on that float even being computed correctly -- it is never read for this field

independent_implementation_statement.verified_by: AST-based import check (ast.walk over each module's own Import/ImportFrom nodes), not a substring search -- substring search on either module's source false-positives on its own docstring, which describes the independence property in prose
independent_implementation_statement.shared_utility_note: Parser B imports qntylab.r1_input_bom.canonical_hash/canonical_bytes (a generic, repo-wide JSON-canonicalization helper with no market-timestamp semantics); Parser A defines its own separate canonical_bytes/canonical_hash. The two _canonical_utc_timestamp/_epoch_to_iso timestamp formatters are separately written, non-shared functions.
